newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch shares hit new record on dollar, Wall Street.
newsitem.headline: Dutch shares hit new record on dollar, Wall Street.

text.p: Dutch shares roared ahead on Wednesday, hitting fresh all-time highs as bourses across Europe rallied behind a surging dollar and firm start to Wall Street.
Surprise overnight news that telcoms firm Koninlijke PTT Nederland (KPN) had launched a 2.7 billion guilder takeover bid for TNT of Australia helped fuel the early advance.
The AEX index closed up 4.98 points at an all-time record of 581.91 points after hitting 583.12 points high earlier. The rise surpassed the previous peak at 577.36 reached on Tuesday.
Dealers said investor mood remained bouyant and Dutch shares could chalk up more gains should U.S. markets rally further.

The market jumped higher early on as news of KPN's bid for TNT of Australia was absorbed. Dealers welcomed the move, saying it gave the Dutch telecom giant more of global position, adding transport and logistics to its core telecoms activity.
KPN shares closed up 1.70 guilders at 60.60, off the earlier higher of 61.40 but still below the year's peak of 68.50.

Dutch PTT said the bid, one of the biggest in Dutch corporate history, did not imply a shift in empahsis away from telecomunications but said the strategy was to position PTT Post strongly ahead of a liberalisation of postal services in Europe, anticipated by the end of the decade.
"KPN held up well after an early rise. The market obviously thinks it's a good deal," one dealer said.
Banking giant ABN AMRO was another strong performer after the announcement after bourse closing on Tuesday that it was looking to spin-off its investment banking arm MeesPierson.

Analysts reckoned the sale could generate up to 2.5 billion guilders and said the move would be viewed positively, ending a glaring overlap in the bank's activities. The shares stormed 2.40 guilders ahead, closing at a year's high of 96.80 guilders.
"It makes sense within ABN, MeesPeirson is something of a duplication. They're often competitors," said one analyst.
Elsewhere, in the market dealers not good buying again for cyclicals with DSM finishing 1.70 up at 172.70 guilders and Hoogovens 1.30 firmer at 64.00 guilders.
The Dutch steel and aluminium maker announced on Tuesday it was in a 50/50 partnership to recapitalise Belgium's Usines Gustave Boel, a move move applauded by analysts on Wednesday.

"We look favourably upon this joint venture for two reasons. Firstly because the joint venture would improve Hoogovens' product mix. Secondly, because this would strengthen Hoogovens' market share in Belgium and France," brokers ING Barings said.
